# Original engineering fixture: mean and squared error

This is project-authored test material, not a course extract or a claim of teaching efficacy.

For observations 1, 2 and 3, define L(c) = ((1-c)^2 + (2-c)^2 + (3-c)^2)/3.
The derivative is L'(c) = 2c - 4. The second derivative is 2, so c=2 is the unique minimum
over real c, and L(2)=2/3. This relies on the three observations having equal weight and on
using squared loss. Absolute loss has a different objective; do not infer this derivation
for that objective. A diagram compares L(1)=5/3, L(2)=2/3 and L(3)=5/3.

No exam priorities, grading weights, paper recommendations or official answers are supplied.
